record.original_question: For each dimension n, does there exist a positive constant epsilon_n such that every open subset of R^n with volume at most epsilon_n admits an embedding into the unit ball that increases the lengths of all curves, equivalently a length-increasing embedding?

evidence.quote: Show that there is ε_n > 0 such that any open set in R^n with volume at most ε_n admits a length-increasing embedding into a unit ball.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a smooth embedding $f:U\to V$ between open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ length-increasing (or expanding) if for every smooth curve $\gamma:[0,1]\to U$ the length of $f\circ\gamma$ is at least the length of $\gamma$; equivalently, $\|Df(x)v\|\ge\|v\|$ for every $x\in U$ and every $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Let $B^n\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ denote the open unit ball.

Question: For each integer $n\ge 2$, does there exist a constant $\varepsilon_n>0$ such that every open set $U\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ with Lebesgue volume $\mathrm{vol}(U)\le\varepsilon_n$ admits a length-increasing embedding $f:U\to B^n$ into the unit ball?
artifact.status_search_result: The "sponge problem" of constructing expanding (length-increasing) embeddings of small-volume open subsets of R^n into the unit ball is a known open problem of Guth, discussed in his work on the width-volume inequality. According to available sources, even the case n=2 remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Width-Volume Inequality (Larry Guth)
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem: for which dimensions n is there a constant ε>0 so that any bounded open set U⊂R^n with volume less than ε admits an expanding embedding into the unit n-ball?
status_evidence.claim: Guth records the question as an open problem and notes he was unable to construct such embeddings even in dimension 2.
